sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Receptor activity assay: FLAG-tagged construct retains full receptor activity of human HYAL2 (PMC1262777, L1).
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly reports a full-length, membrane-anchored HYAL2 construct bearing a FLAG tag at the mature N-terminus, with receptor activity preserved. The topology landmarks confirm signal peptide cleavage after residue 20 (A) and the mature N-terminus at residue 21 (M); Python verification confirms residue_before=A, residue_after=M. Because HYAL2 is GPI-anchored (no TM or intracellular domain in the topology), the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus, making insert_after_residue=20 the unique topology-derived junction. No residue number is named in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Full-length, membrane-anchored human HYAL2 expressed with the native signal peptide (residues 1–20) replaced by a preprotrypsin signal sequence followed by a FLAG peptide tag; the mature protein therefore carries the FLAG at its extracellular N-terminus. HYAL2 is GPI-anchored with no TM domain, so the N-terminus (residue 21) is the sole extracellular terminus and the only possible surface location for this tag.

sources.claim: However, this signal can be replaced with a preprotrypsin signal sequence followed by a Flag peptide tag without affecting the receptor activity of human Hyal2 [ 5 ].

literature_notes: L2 describes the same FLAG-at-N-terminus construct design used in a series of N-terminal deletion mutants to map receptor-activity determinants; it corroborates L1 but does not add a distinct junction or residue, so it does not generate a separate site. No other tag positions (internal loops, C-terminus) are mentioned anywhere in the ledger. HYAL2 is GPI-anchored; the C-terminus (residue 473) is extracellular in principle but no ledger evidence supports a C-terminal tag, so none is proposed.
